sources.entry: cmyflix - Minimalist Plex/Jellyfin alternative to stream video. AGPL-3.0 C/deb

summary.one_liner: cmyflix is a lightweight, C-based "DIY Netflix" that builds JSON databases of local video files and generates static web pages to stream them from any web server.
keywords: stream tv shows on my nas
summary.what_it_does: The program scans a folder of video files and writes JSON databases that store each file's location and metadata. Those databases are then used to generate static HTML pages for TV shows and movies, which can be served by any ordinary web server. The README says it searches for mp4, mkv, ogv and webm files, which are played through HTML5 video. Metadata lookup uses a TMDB API key, and ImageMagick and ffmpeg are listed as requirements. Configuration is read from cmyflix.cfg, looked up next to the binary, in $HOME/.config/cmyflix/, or in /etc/cmyflix/, and a --help menu is available. The project describes itself as a rewrite of an earlier version in C that it says is about 30x faster while keeping almost all functionality. It is intentionally minimal and not designed to be feature-heavy.
use_cases: stream my personal video collection on a NAS
run a simple media library on a Raspberry Pi
generate static TV show and movie pages from local files
serve a home Netflix-style interface from any web server
organize TV show seasons and movie folders with TMDB metadata
how_to_run: Install the build libraries (Ubuntu): libbsd-dev libcjson-dev libcurl4-openssl-dev
Install from source with: make install
Or install the pre-compiled .deb package from the release tab
Create cmyflix.cfg (in the binary folder, $HOME/.config/cmyflix/, or /etc/cmyflix/) and add a TMDB API key
notable: Generates static HTML pages from JSON databases, so it can run behind any web server without a dynamic backend
Rewritten in C; the author says it is about 30x faster than the original version
Deliberately minimal, aimed at low-power boards like Raspberry Pi and Odroid
Expects a strict folder layout: one folder per show with season sub-folders, and one folder per movie
Pre-built .deb package available alongside source builds
caveats: Only mp4, mkv, ogv and webm files are detected, due to HTML5 format support
Requires a TMDB API key and external tools (ImageMagick, ffmpeg)
Expects media in a specific folder structure; the README calls it 'a bit picky'
Explicitly not designed to be feature-rich; the author points users to other solutions for more functionality
The README does not mention built-in authentication; it points to an external option for password protection (link not shown in the text)
